shaNote: builtAtGitSha is the working-tree HEAD when this static library was built, so it always trails the deployed revision by the one commit that carries this file. Use /health.gitSha for the deployed revision and freshness.stale for whether any report here is out of date.
note: Human-readable research reports, rendered from the committed reports/ directory. These characterise the pipeline's operating point and cross-checks on real public TESS data with positive controls -- measurements and method checks, not claims of new planets. Each entry carries a freshness flag from the report-freshness gate; stale reports are marked red both here and in their fragment. Three levels, and they are not interchangeable: `stamped` means only that a report carries a generatedAt timestamp; `verified` means the gate re-hashed at least one recorded input checksum against a file TRACKED IN THIS REPOSITORY and found it unchanged -- so a stranger cloning the repo can re-run the same check; `fullyVerified` means every recorded input was tracked, present and matching. Quote `fullyVerified` as the machine-checked count. A report can be re-hashed on the workstation that built it and still not be verifiable by anyone else: `untrackedInputs` counts checksums over gitignored working files (they matched here, but no clone has those bytes), and `unverifiableInputs` counts paths that are absent here entirely. Both are named on the report page, so exactly what is missing is visible.
